Where the story begins

My interests often begin with a question: how could this work better, and who would it help? Business, technology, economics, and education give me different ways to explore that question. I like the process of learning a skill because I need it, trying an approach, and gradually making something tangible.

This account begins with the experiences I can document from high school. The people and places before those years are part of my story too, but I have kept family history and private details out of this public record.
mexico
Finding my place in Guadalajara

During high school in Guadalajara, much of my involvement centered on Model United Nations, public speaking, and community service. Model UN asked me to research unfamiliar viewpoints, defend a position, listen to competing arguments, and negotiate. It helped me become more comfortable with questions that did not have one obvious answer.

From September 2023 through June 2024, I taught English through Aprendiendo Juntos. Working with adult community members meant adapting to different educational backgrounds and paying attention to whether my explanations were useful. Teaching was an opportunity to practice communication across cultures and to contribute to the community around me.
ohio
Starting again in Ohio

Moving from Guadalajara to Mason after freshman year meant finding my footing in a new school community. I had to introduce myself, get involved, and take part before everything felt familiar. In Mexico, I had found opportunities through diplomacy and service. In Ohio, I began exploring entrepreneurship, technology, and finance more deeply.

Starting again could be uncomfortable, but it also made me more open to interests I might not have discovered otherwise. I became more willing to enter a conversation without knowing everything, ask a question, and learn from the people already doing the work.
building
From ideas to initiatives

MindMate Health gave my interest in entrepreneurship a practical form. I worked on product design, user experience, technology, and business strategy while exploring access to mental wellness resources. Some approaches needed revision; others had to be reconsidered completely. Conversations with mental health professionals helped me recognize the limits of my own understanding.

Helping establish Mason Venture Studio extended that learning beyond my own project. I worked on program structure, operations, and mentor connections while other students developed businesses and nonprofit ideas. Through Uplift Academy Ohio, which I founded in March 2025, I helped create free STEM experiences for younger students. These projects asked different things of me, but all required attention to the people involved.
lead
Learning to lead

At Uplift’s Innovation Camp showcase, students explained their projects to their families. I remember how meaningful it felt to see their ideas receive attention. The volunteer coordination and planning mattered because they made that moment possible.

At Venture Studio, I learned that students needed different kinds of support. One might need help choosing a next step. Another might need an introduction to someone with expertise I did not have. Sometimes the useful response was to ask a question and leave room for the person to work through an answer.

I also became more realistic about my own time. Enthusiasm did not remove the need to set priorities, ask for help, or adjust a commitment. Following through required more than accepting responsibility; it required understanding what that responsibility would demand.
next
What comes next

I am interested in studying business, economics, and finance, and in continuing to explore the connections between technology, psychology, and public policy. Venture capital appeals to me because guidance, resources, or an introduction can help a founder give an idea a chance.

My ambition is to build ventures and help other people build theirs. I am still learning how to do that thoughtfully. What feels clearer now is the question I want to keep asking: can the opportunities I receive become opportunities for other people?
